newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent steadies after posting new nine-month low.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent steadies after posting new nine-month low.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures turned weaker on Thursday afternoon, erasing modest early gains on a combination of technical and fundamental weakness, brokers said.
May Brent dipped to a new nine-month low of $17.60 a barrel after breaking key support at $17.65, the previous lowest point of this year's down move posted on April 4.
By 1432 GMT, the prompt contract steadied to trade at $17.67 a barrel, still eight cents down on Wednesday's settlement.
"There is still quite a bit of crude in the market but a lot of weakness now is coming from the technical perspective," said a broker.

Dealers said a weak opening on NYMEX crude and gasoline and the failure of May Brent to break back above technical resistance at $18.40-$18.50 in the last three trading sessions had set the scene for further losses.
"The market has failed at resistance points for the last couple of days although it has been close to those sort of levels," said a broker.
"There's probably every sign that we will go lower as the day progresses," he added.
Technical analysts pegged the next levels of support at $17.52 and $17.42 a barrel for prompt Brent.
May gas oil followed crude lower, losing $4.00 a tonne to trade at $160.25 by 1451 GMT.
Earlier, the April contract expired $2.25 lower at $160.25 a tonne. Physical deliveries against April would total 1,072 lots, or 107,200 tonnes, an IPE official said on Thursday.
